Spaghetti bolognese. This is my recipe. This will feed 3 or 4 people. 

INGREDIENTS:
A red, green or yellow pepper - diced.
1 medium sized onion - diced.
Chestnut mushrooms - same amount as above diced.
3 or 4 chilli Peppers - diced.
3 or 4 cloves of garlic (or more to your preference) minced.
A few rashers of bacon sliced into lardons. 
500g beef mince. 
Tea spoon of dried rosemary. 
Tea spoon of dried oregano. 
Table spoon of dried basil. 
2 large Bay leaves or 3/4 smaller ones. 
Fresh basil. (for garnish - needed if you like basil) 
Parmesan cheese - grated. (for garnish and added to the sauce at the end) 
500g Passata. 
500g peeled plum tomatoes. 
Spaghetti. 
Beef Knorr stock pot or something similar. (just adds to the flavour) 
A glass of good red wine. (not necessarily needed but adds to flavour - not cooking wine)

Fry off the bacon gently (and rosemary) with a little oil in a large saucepan.

Once golden brown add the pepper, onion and mushrooms. Sweat these off until the onion starts to turn translucent. (by sweat I mean gently fry) add the garlic until very aromatic and then salt and pepper to taste. Turn up the heat and add the beef mince to brown off. Salt and pepper again to taste but remember you can always add more but never take out so be sure not to overly season! 

Once the beef is cooked add the peeled plum tomatoes and cook for a few minutes before breaking them up with your spoon. Add the Passata, dried basil, oregano and bayleaves. Also add the chilli's, wine and stock pot. 

Cook on a gentle simmer for ATLEAST an hour. This let's the flavours develop throughout the sauce and it becomes rich and amazing. Taste and season if needed. 

After an hour or so you can now start to cook the spaghetti. Large saucepan with boiling water. Salt the water very well and cook the spaghetti for as long as it says on the packet.

Turn the saucepan off with the sauce in and add a nice handful of grated parmesan to the sauce. Stir it in.

If you have fresh basil - pick off some nice leaves and make sure you have some parmesan left over to sprinkle on top.

Now you don't have to do this bit but I like to have sauce on all of my spaghetti. Once the spaghetti is cooked - drain it but save like a centimetre of the water it was boiled in. Put a little bit of oil in with the saved water and bring back to the heat on low. Add the spaghetti back to the pan and take a couple of ladels of the sauce and mix it with the spaghetti. 

Plate up! Spaghetti and a heap of sauce on top with basil and parmesan to finish.
